decimal_place_value.title: Decimal place value
decimal_place_value.big_idea: After the decimal point the places are tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths. More digits does not mean bigger: 0.5 is 5 tenths, and 0.25 is only 2 tenths and 5 hundredths.
steps: Line up the two numbers by their decimal points.
If one has fewer digits, add zeros at the end: 0.5 becomes 0.50. This does not change its value.
Compare the tenths digits first. The bigger tenths digit wins.
Only if the tenths are equal, compare the hundredths, and so on.
decimal_place_value.sense_check: Think of money: 0.5 of a rupee is 50 paise, 0.25 of a rupee is 25 paise. 50 paise is more.

adding_decimals.title: Adding and subtracting decimals
adding_decimals.big_idea: You can only add digits that have the same place value. Lining up the decimal points lines up tenths with tenths and hundredths with hundredths.
steps: Write the numbers one under the other with the decimal points in a straight line.
Fill any empty places at the end with 0 so both have the same number of decimal places.
Add or subtract column by column from the right, carrying or borrowing as usual.
Put the decimal point in the answer directly under the other points.
adding_decimals.sense_check: Estimate first: 2.5 + 1.25 is about 2 + 1 = 3, so an answer like 1.5 can't be right.
